blocks.text: The following evening, Eleanor went around the shuttered laboratory building and down the steps into its sunken service yard. She knocked at the basement’s ordinary service door. Inside, something clattered, followed by a hurried scrape of feet.

The workshop above them, where Daniel had built the robot, stood empty. He had secretly returned through the sewers after the police search. Luke’s iron jaws had chewed through a disused drain and the brickwork beyond it, opening a narrow route into a workshop concealed behind the basement’s storage shelves. The opening came out above the sewer water; the workshop floor stayed dry.
Daniel opened the door a few inches. His enormous glasses slipped down his nose. “Eleanor?”
“Are you going to leave me down here?”

He pulled the door open. She stepped over a cable and stopped. Old cups crowded the workbench. A gray film covered the small window high in the wall facing the yard. Something beneath her shoe made a sticky sound.
“This place is filthy.”
Daniel snatched a rag from the bench and rubbed at a dark patch beside the nearest cup. The patch spread. He turned the rag over and tried again.
blocks.alt: Eleanor recoils at the filthy laboratory while a startled Daniel hurriedly wipes a grimy workbench with a rag.

blocks.text: “If you’d telephoned, I could have—”
“I have telephoned. I wanted to see whether you were doing any work.” She looked at the stool he hastily cleared for her. “I’ll stand.”
A metallic click came from behind a tall cabinet.
Luke drifted into the light. His blond spikes nearly brushed the hanging lamp. Beneath his face, the iron jaws opened slightly.
“Uncle Daniel? Who’s—”
Eleanor stepped back so sharply that her handbag struck the doorframe. One hand rose toward her pearls. She stared at the empty air beneath Luke’s jaw.
blocks.alt: Eleanor recoils in horror at Luke’s floating blond head and iron jaws while Daniel tries to explain his nephew’s condition.

blocks.text: “What on earth have you done?”
Daniel dropped the rag. “My nephew. There was an injury, and the treatment—”
“No.” She held up her hand. “Don’t tell me.”
Luke stopped moving. “He was supposed to fix it.”
Eleanor turned away from him. “Daniel. We need to talk.”
“He can stay,” Daniel said. “He won’t interrupt.” Luke looked at his uncle, then hovered beside the cabinet.
“Billy is snooping around,” Eleanor said. “He found your landlord. He took an invoice to that reporter.”
Daniel’s hand closed around the rag. “I told you he was helping those Defenders.”
“And I told him to stop. That won’t keep him out of your affairs for long.” She lowered her voice. “You need to fast-track Project Skyfall.”
Luke moved a little closer. “What’s Project Skyfall?”
Daniel glanced at him. “Stay over there.”
“How much longer?” Eleanor asked.
“I’ve had interruptions. The robot—”
“Is lying in pieces. I’m asking about Skyfall.”
Daniel pushed the old cups farther down the bench. “I need money.”
Eleanor opened her handbag. She took out a folded stack of bills and held it beyond the greasy edge of the counter.
“The rent. Put it in the landlord’s hand.”
Daniel reached for the money. She kept hold of it until he looked up.
“From now on, no paper trails between us. No checks. No invoices sent to my house. We’ll do everything with cash.”
He nodded. She released the bills.
blocks.alt: Eleanor hands Daniel a stack of cash in his cluttered laboratory while Luke, a floating blond head with iron jaws, watches from beside a cabinet.

blocks.text: “The landlord will still keep his accounts,” Daniel said. “And if I stop paying, he’ll take the keys. I need the upstairs kept shut.”
“Then let them show you paid him. Keep my name out of it.” She closed her handbag. “And get back to work.”
Luke watched Daniel fold the money into his coat pocket. “Does Skyfall have anything to do with getting my body back?”
Daniel picked up the rag again. “Not now, Luke.”
Eleanor stepped around the cable on her way out. At the door, her eyes passed over Luke’s floating face. She looked away before he could ask her anything.
“Clean this place,” she said.
Daniel shut the door behind her. Luke waited beside the cabinet while his uncle counted the bills.
“What is it?” Luke asked once more.
Daniel lost his place in the count and began again. Luke stayed where he was. Nobody had answered him.
